successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: the Dauphiné and the Faucigny, transferred by Humbert II to the future Charles V ('a distinctive polity, not incorporated into the French kingdom') under the Treaty of Romans; the Cliopatria Kingdom…

rulers.name: Humbert I (Baron of La Tour du Pin)
Charles (the future Charles V), first Valois dauphin

ledger.x: 1260: first year of the Cliopatria shape of the Dauphiné of Viennois, centred on Grenoble; the pages give no founding year.
1268: the Faucigny comes to the Dauphin's wife.
16 July 1349: Humbert II hands the Dauphiné to the future Charles V.
1351: last year of the Cliopatria Dauphiné shape; the Kingdom of France shape holds Grenoble from 1352.

wars.name: War of Humbert II with Aymon of Savoy
wars.outcome: Humbert II inherited the Dauphiné in 1333 while at war with Aymon, Count of Savoy; Philip VI arranged a truce within a year.

wars.name: Savoyard dispute over the Faucigny
wars.outcome: Amadeus VI of Savoy challenged the French purchase, defeated the French in 1354 and obtained the Faucigny under the Treaty of Paris (1355).

certainty.note: The frontiers with Savoy, the Provence marquisate and the Rhône bishoprics are feudal and approximate; no treaty line before the Treaty of Paris of 1355.
